H1.qualification: Implementation verified by source and a bounded mock-execution probe; no reviewer-run PostgreSQL deadlock proof.
H1.verified: After packaging-head locking and before readiness_in, select explicitly locks {selector} union human_principals(run.observation_refs). The existing helper sorts the complete set and takes FOR UPDATE per principal. Readiness's assessor-only re-locks and admit's selector re-lock therefore target already-held locks. This removes the previously described late-selector grant cycle for arbitrary principal names, including disjoint-master writers.
H1.multi_principal_judgment: The fix is correct by construction; a full multi-principal PG fixture is not required to establish that the union and sorted helper eliminate this particular inversion. A reviewer inline probe evaluated the actual select AST's principals expression and called the real lock_grant_heads with a recording session: selector a/assessor z and selector z/assessor a both issued a then z; a three-principal case issued a, m, z. This does not exercise PG scheduling. The persisted spy has selector == assessor == ACTOR and sorts the input for its own log, so it would also pass after replacing the union with selector-only or assessor-only locking. Add a distinct-selector/assessor regression, with selector sorting before the assessor; include disjoint masters in the PG test if claiming reproduction/closure of the historical interleaving. That remaining test requirement is tracked under M2, not as an unfixed runtime H1.

M1.qualification: Fresh preview/selection implementation closed; persisted tamper-after-preview service regressions still absent.
M1.verified: Both preview creation and fresh selection call resolve_package_evidence. It loads the exact candidate revision, verifies its stored/requested digest, calls the shared payload/closure/lineage verifier, loads the repository-verified packaging observation and its run, resolves the verified V2 profile, recomputes the constraint snapshot, compares candidate/observation snapshots and base-subject binding, checks the full five-column slot scope, and validates variants and exact waivers. Fresh selection also compares the resolved run ID and recomputed observation digest with the preview. Existing run-digest and disposition-digest/current-head checks remain. Replay intentionally returns the verified historical receipt before resolving live package evidence.
M1.probe: With mocked repository reads and real candidate/observation/policy contracts and verifier functions, a coherent package resolved; wrong slot, missing group choice, stray waiver, tampered candidate and wrong observation snapshot refused. This is bounded function-level evidence, not real DB tamper-after-preview coverage.

M2.improvement: New Event gates pause a real writer with locks held, then start a contender and poll pg_stat_activity. Pair tests now exist for disposition in both orders, seal, publication and another selection. This is meaningful progress over gather-only races. The publication repository test can exercise a genuine profile FOR UPDATE waiting behind selection's FOR SHARE.
remaining_scenarios: wait_for_lock_waiter counts any Lock waiter in the entire database, excluding only its own backend. It neither identifies the contender PID nor checks pg_blocking_pids against the gated writer, target relation or requested/held mode. An unrelated test/backend can satisfy it. Thus the tests cannot assert which waiter or lock was observed.

In selection-first disposition, the gate is after selection has locked the ACTOR grant. issue() still needs authorize_disposition(), whose separate lease transaction locks the same ACTOR grant before the owning disposition write transaction starts. The observed wait can therefore be lease issuance, not disposition-head FOR UPDATE behind selection's FOR SHARE. Pre-authorize the contender before pausing selection.

Reverse disposition, run-seal and same-slot selection fixtures share master rows. They can block at the first no-op master UPDATE before reaching run/disposition/packaging heads. In particular the test named waits_on_the_slot_head does not establish that the slot lock was reached. Removing later row locks could leave these tests passing.

The publication case calls the repository test append helper with synthetic custody and omits ProfilePublicationService's activated custodian/grant admission. It proves only the narrower repository/profile-head interaction; it does not prove the full publication writer pair.

Only disposition has both controlled writer orders. Seal-first refusal is tested sequentially by newer_run, not as a blocked selection. Publication-first invalidation is absent. The principal-order spy has no distinct principals and cannot detect dropping either side of the union.

The waiter helper contains asyncio.sleep(0.05), whereas design section 4 explicitly requires no sleeps. Outcome sequencing uses Events, but polling still needs an explicit accepted exception or a compliant observation seam.
M2.fix: Bind each observation to contender and blocker backend PIDs, assert pg_blocking_pids and the intended lock/mode or instrument the exact lock seam; pre-issue leases; arrange or separately probe the head-level conflicts so common master locks do not mask them. Exercise the actual publication service or label its repository-only limit and add the real service pair. Add the missing reverse-currentness orders and a distinct-principal union regression. Retain all required B3 writer-pair evidence before claiming the section 4 gate closed.

M3.improvement: Added meaningful exact allowed waiver, absent/wrong-rule waiver, unwaivable integrity failure, another-command lease, expired lease, newer run, zero/multiple/unknown alternatives, selection-command conflict and concurrent identical-command cases. Collection independently confirms 26 PG cases. Builder reports all 26 passed on PG16; reviewer execution was blocked before the first body.
remaining_scenarios: The +31s database_now seam tests lease admission expiry only. There is no expired-preview selection test, no independent disposition-expiry test, and no assertion that preview expiry is capped by a shorter disposition. Pure contract window validation does not cover these service decisions.

No stale master, invalidating profile publication, or wrong source/cohort/surface/project slot refusal is persisted at the B3 service boundary. The publication test exercises successful selection before a later publication, not refusal when publication wins.

The cross-request lease test changes only command_id while reusing the same preview. It does not prove a lease for preview A cannot authorize preview B's changed choices/waivers, nor the exact stored-lease/request/preview digest checks independently.

No B3 grant revocation/sequence change after lease issuance, API-key/auth-disabled refusal, crash-after-lease, or candidate/lineage/observation tamper-after-preview test. No positive multi-group selection; the new group test uses one group and stops at preview.

Waiver refusal tests run at preview. They do not exercise changed checked evidence at fresh selection; extra/partial multi-finding coverage is not persisted. Several refusals also omit no-selection/no-head assertions, and _counts checks head row count rather than an existing head's version/selection identity.
M3.fix: Add focused service RED tests for the outstanding design section 8 cases, particularly independent preview/disposition expiry, stale master/profile, slot confusion, changed-preview/waiver lease binding and tamper after preview. Assert no selection and no change to an existing packaging head on refusal. Add distinct multi-group and grant-change cases. Keep A6 tests as regression evidence for A6, not substitutes for the copied B3 custodian and new resolver.

new_findings_note: No additional runtime defect confirmed in the bounded delta. Newly identified weaknesses in the added waiter/spy tests are detailed under the still-open M2/M3 rather than double-counted as new findings.
